<thought>We need to determine the number of carbonyl (C=O) groups in the unknown compound. The available tools can provide spectroscopic data for the sample at hand. The carbon NMR spectrum will show signals in the typical carbonyl region (≈190–220 ppm). By counting how many distinct peaks appear in that region, we can infer the number of carbonyl carbons, which corresponds to the number of C=O groups. Therefore, I will request the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample.</thought>
